Three things:

  1. Read EVERY label. Short labels are best, but since about 2004 the food industry has to report a certain ppm of gluten containing stuff. No oatmeal. Often contaminated. No soy. No soy oil, or Lecithin.

  2. Get the celiac blood test. This is how my ex's problems were found--a simple test of the blood. Even if you aren't celiac, you may still be "sensitive." Don't buy media hype that it's "not that common." It's all too common. Some people are not affected by meats where animals are fed grains. My son's case was extreme.

  3. This dieting stuff is really a bitch until you're used to it, but it's worth it. My grandkids are healthy, my son is healthy, and I think my ex is healthy. Being able to do stuff again and know what you can and can't eat is a huge help. Once things are in balance for you again (took us about 2 years with my ex), you will feel normal. That's worth just about everything. Of course, if your problem is not celiac, you may have to restrict other things, such as milk (lactose intolerance goes along with celiac sometimes, other times is by itself). And DON'T trust "just any physician." Lots of these folks don't know what they are talking about, and will just prescribe palliative medicines, which is all that are advertised on the media anyway. The typical MD's never found my ex's problem. They tested her for everything else, but not that. I finally sent her to a nutrition doc (he was an MD), who found the problem the first time she got tested.
